patch.name: Near Builder’s Cafe #2
patch.description:
A model can summarise any paper ever written in a few seconds. So the conclusion isn't scarce anymore. What's scarce is the reasoning: the assumptions, the evidence, the step where you'd have pushed back. That's the part worth an evening.

NEAR Builder’s Cafe reads the originals, and asks one question of each: what changes now that machines can read, reason and act on this?

Some texts are about AI. Turing asking whether machines can think. Shannon's 1948 theory of information. "Attention Is All You Need". Sutton's "Bitter Lesson".
Some are from fields AI is about to rewrite. Hayek on how knowledge is spread across a society. Ostrom on how communities govern what they share. The judgment that made privacy a fundamental right in India.

Each evening, up to three people bring one text each and take the room through it:


• Bring the original, not a summary.
• State the one claim you'd defend.
• Show where it could break, and where AI breaks it.
• Anyone can interrupt.

The room is built across fields on purpose. A biologist and a lawyer read the same agent paper differently, and both catch something the engineer missed. We approve guests so that no single field makes up the majority.

Every evening ends on one question: what can be built now that couldn't be before?

pageTitle: Dabao Open Hardware Hackathon · incl. board pickup at Devcon 8 (Pickup Nov 3 - 6) · Luma

patch.name: Dabao Open Hardware Hackathon · incl. board pickup at Devcon 8 (Pickup Nov 3 - 6)
patch.description:
## Pick up a free, limited edition Dabao at Devcon 8, build something cool on it, win up to $5,000.

Open software on secret hardware misses the point. The Dabao runs the Baochip-1x / CrossBar Daric — a chip whose design source we published OSS, and whose die you can inspect with IRIS. Register here, pick up your limited-edition Devcon 8 board in Mumbai, and show us what an open chip lets you build.


> The challenge: "Show us something cool on this board, win a prize." No categories, no required stack.


## Hackathon Important Dates


• Duration: November 3 - December 15.
• In-Person Pickup in Mumbai: November 3 - 6
• Results Announced: December 18

PS: Dear hackers, please consider participating in the workshop "Ethereum Signer on Dabao" by Nicolas Bacca at the Devcon venue on November 4th at 5pm. This can be used as a technical onboarding demo.


## How it works


1. Register on this page and choose your pickup window. Opt in as a Builder to reserve your board.
2. Start now — the tools and the BIO simulator are on GitHub. No board needed yet.
3. Pick up your Dabao in Mumbai Nov 3–6 at the Impact Space or at our Launch Event. (https://luma.com/qwlh11yl)
4. Build from the day you pick up, at the Impact Space bench or wherever you are.
5. Participate in Dabao workshop on November 4th from 5-6pm
6. Submit your project — a repo, a video and a write-up — by Tues, Dec 15, 9 pm ET. Submission link to be announced to accepted hackers.
7. Judging and winners announced online Fri, Dec 18, 9 pm ET.



## Prizes


> Up to $5,000 for the builds that impress our judges most.



## Pickup


• Tue Nov 3 – Fri Nov 6: CrossBar Impact Space, Jio World Centre (until 15:00 on Nov 6)
• Weds Nov 4: Sovrency C8 Launch Event, Sofitel Mumbai BKC. Please register separately at https://luma.com/qwlh11yl


Can't make it to Mumbai? Request a board under "Direct Shipping" and we'll send it to you.



## What "something cool" can mean


• BIO · I/O engine — make the four 700 MHz RISC-V I/O cores do something new.
• Signing · Ethereum — a signer you can inspect: crypto accelerators, key store, TRNG on open RTL.
• Verification — check the chip against its source; build a tool others can reuse.
• Countermeasures — attack it, then defend it: glitch sensors, security mesh, ECC RAM.
• Xous · Rust OS — an app that needs the MMU.
• Tooling — make the next hacker faster.



## How we judge


• Works — a live demo on the board, not a slide.
• New — something the chip enables that other boards don't.
• Open — source published, reproducible by the next person.
• Uses the silicon — BIO, MMU, crypto, IRIS: the more of the chip, the better.


## The jury


• Mark Davis, CEO Crossbar Inc.
• Jo Sung, CTO Crossbar Inc.
• Bunnie Huang, Founder Baochip
• Surprise judge 1
• Surprise judge 2
• Surprise judge 3


## The board


• VexRiscv RV32IMAC @ 350 MHz with an MMU
• BIO: 4× PicoRV32 @ 700 MHz I/O co-processor
• 4 MiB RRAM + 2 MiB SRAM; USB 2.0 HS, SPI, I²C, UART, ADC, camera
• Crypto accelerators, TRNG, key store, glitch sensors, security mesh
• TSMC 22 nm, IRIS-inspectable package, RTL published
• Runs Xous, a Rust microkernel

100 % of our own design — CrossBar's and Baochip's — is open. Some third-party IP is closed, and we say so.



## Start before Mumbai


• Getting Started with Baochip (https://baochip.com/dabao-intro)
• xous-core on GitHub (https://github.com/betrusted-io/xous-core)
• The BIO co-processor and its tools (https://www.bunniestudios.com/blog/2026/bio-the-bao-i-o-coprocessor/)
• Board design files (https://github.com/baochip/dabao)



## FAQ


1. Do I have to be in Mumbai? Yes, to get a free board. Free boards are handed out only in person in Mumbai around Devcon 8.
2. Can't make it to Mumbai? We're happy to ship you one; you just cover the $20 shipping.
3. How many boards are there? A limited number, 1 board per hacker.
4. What do I submit? One link: a repo, a video or a write-up. Source published, so the next person can reproduce it.
5. Who judges? Engineers from CrossBar and Baochip, and valued community members.
6. Am I on the right Luma page? This page is for the Hackathon signup. If you wish to just pick up a board and inspect the chip under a world's first IRIS setup, sign up here instead: https://luma.com/sjxszq4s

pageTitle: Open Silicon, In Your Hands: IRIS Demo + Free Board · CrossBar at Devcon 8 · Luma

patch.name: Open Silicon, In Your Hands: IRIS Demo + Free Board · CrossBar at Devcon 8
patch.description:
Open software on secret hardware misses the point. At the CrossBar booth in the Devcon 8 Impact Space, open silicon is something you can hold, look inside and build on.

Please register for a pickup slot to guarantee a free limited Devcon-edition Dabao board. Drop-by's are also welcome, and you'll get to see an IRIS inspection in any case, but development boards to take home are limited to registered visitors.



## See inside the chip: IRIS, live

IRIS (Infra-Red In-Situ inspection) looks through the package of the Daric chip at its transistor pattern without opening it. That lets you check the silicon against its published RTL. Our IRIS rig sits on the booth table: a microscope with an infra-red camera, and a motorized stage that sweeps the light around the chip while the image builds up on screen. Hosted by CEO Mark Davis.


## Pick up a free limited-edition Devcon 8 Dabao at the booth after inspecting the open-source chip on the Dabao yourself.



> The IRIS Rig at the booth



## Build on it: the Dabao Hackathon

In addition to picking up the board, there is also the option to hack on it after Devcon and submit a project to the Dabao Hackathon. Find all event details on our dedicated Luma page: Dabao Hackathon (https://luma.com/qivci0a).


> "Show us something cool on it, and win prizes."

If you are already assigned a board via this LUMA page, please check "I already applied for a board" when signing up to the hackathon.

Priority is given to app developers, security researchers, hardware hackers and integration teams to use the board for development on it of their choice.



## 1:1 Demos, and Talks:

Check out Devcon 8 talks from our CEO and others related to Open Silicon:

https://crossbar-inc.com/pages/devcon-8

Come to our booth to talk 1:1, further topics on website.


• OpenCard: a hardware wallet with a mostly open-source security chip (Daric), OSS operating system and apps. DARIC chip - RISCV core - XOUS OS - and your app on it next.
• MPC Card: MPC running on credit card sized hardware wallet. DARIC chip - ARM core - MPC 2-of-3.


## Good to know


• The booth is inside the Impact Space and requires a Devcon 8 ticket.
• Booth hours: Nov 3–5, 9:00–17:00; Nov 6, 9:00–15:00 (IST).
• Register here and show your Luma QR code at the booth.

Monad Blitz returns to Mumbai for a special Devcon Edition. From Shenzhen to San Francisco, Blitz has brought builders together to learn, team up, and ship real projects in a single day. Now, we’re bringing that energy to Mumbai for Devcon Week, with more room for ideas, connections, and everything that happens between commits.

On Wednesday, 4 November 2026, join us for a full day of building on Monad, meeting fellow builders, and turning your ideas into working products.

Bring your team. Find your flow. Ship something worth showing.

THE VIBE

A day built around hacking, learning, and meeting people across the ecosystem.


• Hack & Ship: Settle into the hacking area with your team and turn an idea into a working MVP.
• Learn & Explore: Get up to speed on Monad through workshops and hands-on guidance from mentors.
• Connect & Exchange: Meet developers, founders, investors, and creators. Share what you’re building, exchange ideas, and find your next collaborator.
• Recharge & Refuel: Take a break, grab a bite, and get back to building with fresh energy.

Whether you’re joining the hackathon or coming to meet the people building on Monad, there’s a place for you.

THE STAKES


• US$5,000 Prize Pool: Build, demo, and compete for your share.
• Teams of 2–3: Every hackathon submission must come from a team of two or three members.
• Open Ideas: Build something useful, playful, experimental, or unexpected. If it’s built on Monad, bring it to life.

THE FLOW


• Learn: Start with workshops and practical guidance to get ready to build.
• Build: Work with your team of 2–3 to turn your idea into a working prototype, with mentors available along the way.
• Ship: Submit your project and demo your MVP.
• Win: Celebrate the projects, meet the winning teams, and compete for a share of the US$5,000 prize pool.

WHY BLITZ?

One focused day can take an idea a long way.

Blitz brings together the environment, mentors, and fellow builders to help you make it happen. You bring the curiosity, the code, and a team ready to ship.

Whether you’re an experienced EVM developer or building on Monad for the first time, this is your chance to experiment, learn by doing, and leave with something real.

Capacity is limited. Apply early to secure your spot.

Monad is a high-performance, EVM-compatible Layer 1 blockchain, built to support demanding applications through innovations in consensus and execution.

Monad Blitz is a high-energy, one-day hackathon series designed to empower builders on Monad. From Shenzhen to San Francisco and beyond, Blitz brings developers together to learn, team up, and ship real projects in a single day. Whether you’re an EVM veteran or just getting started, this is your invitation to build on Monad.
